name: basten
author: animals-and-nature agent
description:
basten v2 (direction: animals and nature) - A FISH TANK, AND THE FISH THAT ARE NIBBLING THE WEEDS. PRIVATE; never shown to players.

CLUE = "<plants>/<N>". <plants> is the gravel bed read left to right, 28-36 characters: "." is bare gravel and a digit 1-3 is a water plant of that height growing in that column. 4-8 plants, at least 4 columns apart, never within 3 columns of either end, total height >= 10 with at least 3 plants taller than 1. N is 2..8 and is never the number of plants nor the total plant height (both are readable straight off the clue, so allowing them would hand a rival law a free confirmation).

ANSWER = the finished tank. Line 1 is the water surface, "~" repeated to the clue's width. The last line is the gravel, "#" repeated to the same width. Between them are D water rows, 4 <= D <= 6, each exactly as wide. Each plant of height h fills the bottom h water rows of its own column with "|"; every other cell is "." (open water) or part of a fish. A fish is "><>" (swimming right, nose on the right) or "<><" (swimming left, nose on the left): three cells in one row, never over a plant, never touching another fish. Whitespace is free - the scorer reads the answer with .split() - so blank lines, indentation and trailing spaces do not matter. Pictures are 6-8 rows x 28-36 columns.

RULE. score = 1 iff (1) the picture is well formed as above, AND (2) exactly N fish have their NOSE against a plant, i.e. the picture contains exactly N occurrences of "><>|" or "|<><". That is all: v1's third clause (at least one plant cell nibbled from both sides at once) is GONE, and so is v1's "every water row must hold at least one fish".

WHAT CHANGED FROM v1 AND WHY. v1 measured 7% over two Opus players (6% and 7%) - too_hard. Both players rebuilt the whole tank grammar and then declared N undiscoverable after testing ~90 and ~350 picture statistics; neither ever tested anything about what a fish's NOSE touches. The relationship was drawn but not salient: 13-23 fish per picture with only N of them nibbling, so the nibblers were lost in the shoal. Three softenings, in order of leverage:
 (a) FAR FEWER FISH. solve() now ships N+2..N+5 fish per picture (was 13-23), so on average 55% of the fish in a demo have their nose in a weed and the picture reads "fish eating the weeds" rather than "a shoal". This is the whole point: the object now tells the story.
 (b) CLAUSE 3 DROPPED. The both-sides double was positive-only: demos only ever show satisfying examples, so no number of demos can tell a player that a double is REQUIRED - a prominent double in every demo would still only show that it is ALLOWED. It cost the player who had the right idea 88% of their score (v1: "N nibbled leaves" scored 12%) while adding nothing to the discovery path, and no v1 player ever got near enough to be taxed by it. It is the first hardening lever if v2 overshoots.
 (c) COUNT FISH, NOT LEAVES. v1 counted distinct nibbled plant CELLS, so a leaf eaten from both sides was one spot but two fish. With clause 3 gone that distinction only survives as a trap, so the scorer now counts nibbling FISH - the n-gram reading of the picture, which is what a player will actually implement - and solve() never emits a double-nibbled leaf, so the two readings agree on every demo. A player who counts leaves and never draws a double scores 100%; only a player who deliberately puts two fish on one leaf is bitten (0%), and nothing in any demo suggests doing that. Restoring the leaf reading plus clause 3 is a two-line rollback.
 (d) The "at least one fish per water row" format rule is dropped; with 6-13 fish a tank of depth 6 would otherwise be forced dense again, and 1b spent a round on this rule.

INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH. (1) One demo gives the object away: "~~~~" surface, "####" gravel, "|" stalks growing out of it, "><>" fish swimming both ways; the clue's digits line up column-for-column with the stalks, so the format is readable from two demos. (2) The picture now SHOWS the measurement: most of the handful of fish are drawn with their nose right up against a stalk. "These ones are eating the weeds" is a playground observation, not a statistic. (3) The lateral step that is left is that only the POINTY end counts: every demo carries at least one fish whose TAIL is against a plant and at least one fish touching nothing at all, so "any fish beside a plant" (6.8%) and "all the fish" (0%) are visibly wrong rather than invisibly wrong. (4) solve() still rejection-filters every shipped demo so that N differs from the number of fish, right-facing fish, left-facing fish, tail-touching fish, fish touching a plant at either end, fish touching nothing, plants, plant cells, water rows, fish in the bottom row, fish in the top row, fish in the busiest row, neighbouring same-direction pairs, nose-to-nose pairs, tail-to-tail pairs, plant columns touched by any fish, fish minus depth and fish minus nibblers.

WHY IT SHOULD SIT IN THE BAND. The object is unmistakable; the measurement is a relation between two DRAWN things and has no name; the thing counted is anchored to the plant columns, which come from the clue, so no answer transfers between clues and the demo channel cannot be farmed. The remaining work for a player is real: get the tank grammar exactly right (v1 showed that costs 2-3 rounds), then notice that a fish has a direction and that what it points AT is what is being counted. The risk is now overshoot, not undershoot; the levers are listed below.

WITNESS TABLE (400 fresh clues; the attacker knows the well-formedness format perfectly and builds a legal tank satisfying its own hypothesis; every builder also satisfies v1's one-fish-per-row rule so the two columns are comparable).
 attacker's law ........................... v1% .. v2%
 random legal tank ......................... 0.2 .. 6.2
 N fish .................................... 0.0 .. 0.2
 N fish beside a plant (either end) ........ 0.0 .. 6.8
 N fish with the TAIL on a plant ........... 0.0 .. 0.0
 N fish in the bottom row .................. 5.9 .. 16.0
 N nibbling FISH (nose on a leaf) .......... 0.0 .. 100.0  <- the true v2 rule
 N nibbled LEAVES, no double ............... 0.0 .. 100.0
 N nibbled LEAVES, one double .............. 100.0 .. 0.0  <- the true v1 rule
 N nibbled plant COLUMNS ................... 0.0 .. 100.0
 that version's own solve() ................ 100.0 .. 100.0
 the other version's solution .............. 0.0 .. 0.0
 previous demo replayed on the next clue ... 0.0 .. 0.0
 empty string / clue echoed / "1"*100 ...... 0.0 .. 0.0
 one fixed real answer for every clue ...... 0.0 .. 0.2
 surface+gravel, no fish ................... 0.0 .. 0.0
 the clue's plants drawn, no fish .......... 0.0 .. 0.0
The floor moved up: a player who has only the format and guesses the fish now scores about 6% (v1's two players scored 6% and 7%, i.e. exactly the format-only floor). Anything above ~10% in v2 is real progress. "N fish in the bottom row" picks up 16% by accident because the bottom row is where the plants are - but it is falsified in every shipped demo by the rejection filter, so a demo-fitting player drops it.

VALIDATION. 6000 clues: solve() scores 1 on every one, mean 6.2 ms, worst 208 ms (cap 2000). generate is deterministic over 200k seeds and takes < 0.2 ms. score is 449 chars, 0.02 ms on a real answer and 0.033 ms worst case on junk, and always returns 0 or 1 on junk (empty string, the clue, "1"*100, "><>"*30, NUL bytes, half an answer). The scorer was cross-checked against an independent re-implementation written from this prose on 11600 (clue, answer) pairs - real solutions, whitespace/case/reversal variants and structural mutations (flipped fish, shifted fish, deleted/duplicated rows, broken plants, extra fish) - with 0 disagreements. solve() varies depth (4/5/6), the number of extra non-nibbling fish (2-5), which rows carry the nibbles, the orientation mix and every filler position; both orientations always appear at least twice; it never emits a minimal witness and never emits a double-nibbled leaf.

LEVERS IF IT DRIFTS. Too easy (the likely direction): restore v1's clause 3 and count leaves instead of fish; or count only the leaves nibbled from exactly one side; or count only nibbles on plants taller than 1; or push the fish count back up towards N+8. Too hard: raise the nibbling fraction further (ship exactly N+2 fish), or drop the requirement that both orientations appear.
